reference_title: California Trenching and Shoring Manual (Caltrans, June 2011, Revision 2 - July 2025)

sections.title: Effective Pile Width and Soil Arching
sections.summary: For cantilever (unrestrained) soldier piles, the effective width d is the pile dimension parallel to the wall (driven/gravel-backfilled), or the drilled-hole diameter when 4-sack+ concrete is used below the excavation. Soil arching increases the effective width for PASSIVE resistance below the excavation - up to 3x for granular soil (arching factor f = 0.08*phi, capped at 3) and up to 2x for cohesive soil (Figure 7-4, 1 to 2). The adjusted width cannot exceed the pile spacing; active loads behind the pile use only the effective width.
sections.body: The effective width (d) of a soldier pile is generally the dimension taken parallel to the line of the wall for driven piles or drilled piles backfilled with non-concrete material (e.g. gravel); it may be taken as the diameter of the drilled hole when 4-sack or better concrete is used below the excavation line. Soil arching can greatly increase the effective width for passive resistance below the excavation (Figure 7-3). Passive resistance in front of an isolated pile is three-dimensional and is adjusted for arching beyond the effective width. For granular soils the soil arching factor f = 0.08*phi, limited to 3 (i.e. up to 3x; Eq. 7-2-1), and the Adjusted Pile Width = Effective Width * f, limited to the actual pile spacing (Eq. 7-2-2). The arching capability for cohesive soil ranges between 1 and 2 (Figure 7-4). Below the excavation depth the adjusted pile width is used for passive resistance in front of the pile; any active loadings (including surcharge) on the back of the pile below the excavation use only the effective width, fixing the arching factor at 1. The adjusted pile width cannot exceed the pile spacing.
key_points: Effective width = pile dimension parallel to the wall (or drilled-hole dia. with 4-sack+ concrete)
Granular arching factor f = 0.08*phi, capped at 3 (up to 3x effective width) - Eq. 7-2-1
Adjusted pile width = effective width * f, limited to the pile spacing - Eq. 7-2-2
Adjusted width is for PASSIVE resistance below the excavation only
Active loads behind the pile use the effective width (arching factor = 1)

equations.description: Granular soil arching capability factor f = 0.08*phi, limited to 3.
Adjusted pile width = effective width * f, limited to the actual pile spacing.

sections.title: System Deflection and Point of Fixity
sections.summary: The point of fixity (zero deflection) below the excavation line is a significant analysis assumption affecting embedment, shear, moment and deflection; it is a percentage of the embedment depth D from 0 to 0.75D, and 0.25D may be assumed for unrestrained shoring in most stiff to medium dense soils (the SC Trenching & Shoring Check Program default), a greater value for loose sand or soft clay. Deflection calculations are required for any shoring adjacent to the railroad or high-risk structures; apart from the railroad (Chapter 9) there are no guidelines on maximum allowable lateral deflection.
sections.body: The point of fixity, or point of zero deflection, of the shoring support of a cantilevered system is a significant analysis assumption. The point of fixity below the excavation line (Figure 7-5) affects the pile embedment, shears, moments, and deflection. It is defined as a percentage of the embedment depth D, varying from 0 to 0.75D. For unrestrained shoring systems in most stiff to medium dense soils, a value of 0.25D may be assumed; this is the default in the Structure Construction (SC) Trenching & Shoring Check Program. A greater value may be used for loose sand or soft clay. The total deflection combines bending of the structural member and movement (rotation) of the system within its embedded portion. Deflection calculations are required for any shoring system adjacent to the railroad or high-risk structures. The allowable deflection is inversely proportional to the sensitivity to movement of what is being shored, and the degree of analysis is up to the Engineer's judgment. Except for the railroad (Chapter 9), there are no guidelines on the maximum allowable lateral deflection; for other high-risk structures allowable deflections are on a case-by-case basis. Deflections are normally approximated by standard beam analysis (double integration of the moment diagram, or moment-area from the top of the pile to a depth D below the dredge line), which does not account for rotation of a cantilever or long-term ground-anchor movement; for a realistic deflection a soil-structure interaction analysis (p-y or finite element) must be performed, which is beyond the scope of the manual (contact the SC Falsework Engineer).
key_points: Point of fixity = fraction of embedment depth D (0 to 0.75D)
0.25D may be assumed for most stiff to medium dense soils (SC T&S Check Program default)
A greater value may be used for loose sand or soft clay
Affects embedment, shear, moment, and deflection of the cantilever
Deflection calculations are required for any shoring system adjacent to the railroad or high-risk structures
Except for the railroad (Chapter 9) there are no guidelines on maximum allowable lateral deflection; other high-risk structures case by case

sections.title: Lateral Earth Pressures for Unrestrained Shoring (Rigorous and Simplified)
sections.summary: Cantilever walls are analyzed assuming the vertical member rotates at point O, a depth D0 below the excavation line, by the Rigorous Method (1984 USS Steel Sheet Piling Design Manual; combined active and passive idealized loading extending below O to the pile tip) or the Simplified Method (AASHTO / NCHRP 611). In the Simplified Method (7-5.02), a force R at O replaces the net pressure below O; D0 is found by moments about O and increased 20 percent (D = 1.2*D0, AASHTO 3.11.5.6) to approximate the total embedment. The 20 percent increase is not a factor of safety; it accounts for rotation of the wall length below point O.
sections.body: All shoring is designed for lateral earth pressure, water pressure, and surcharge. The Simplified Method for cantilevers is built on AASHTO and TRB NCHRP Report 611 equations; the Conventional Method of the 1984 USS Steel Sheet Piling Design Manual is presented as the Rigorous Method (a reintroduced pre-2006 practice), which produces a more refined analysis (Section 4-1). Cantilever walls are analyzed by assuming the vertical member rotates at point O, at the distance D0 below the excavation line (Figure 7-7); both methods solve for the embedment depth by balancing the moments driving the system into the excavation against the resisting moments. Rigorous Method (7-5.01): the idealized load distribution (Figure 7-8) combines active and passive pressure and extends below point O down to the tip of the pile; sheet piles and soldier piles have different below-excavation distributions due to pile spacing and effective width (Figures 7-9, 7-10); it solves for embedment depth D, maximum shear, maximum moment and deflection. Simplified Method (7-5.02, Figure 7-11): force R is assumed at point O to compensate the resultant net active and passive pressure below O. The calculated depth D is determined by increasing D0 by 20 percent to approximate the total embedment depth; the 20 percent increase is not a factor of safety, it accounts for the rotation of the length of wall element below point O (D = 1.2D0, AASHTO 3.11.5.6). Procedure: (1) calculate active/passive pressure to point O at depth D0; (2) take moments about O to eliminate R and determine D0; (3) increase D0 by 20 percent (D = 1.2 D0); (4) calculate R by summation of horizontal forces (R <= 0; if R is larger than zero, increase D); (5) calculate Mmax and Vmax; (6) check the lagging and other members (Chapter 6).
key_points: Cantilever methods: Rigorous (1984 USS Steel) and Simplified (AASHTO / NCHRP 611)
Rigorous idealized loading combines active + passive pressure extending below point O to the pile tip
Simplified: force R at point O; solve D0 by moments about O, then D = 1.2*D0 (AASHTO 3.11.5.6)
The 20% increase (D = 1.2*D0) is not a factor of safety - it accounts for rotation below point O
Simplified: R by summation of horizontal forces must be <= 0; if R > 0, increase D
Check max shear, max moment, deflection, then the lagging and other members

equations.description: Simplified Method (Section 7-5.02): total embedment depth D = 1.2*D0, D0 the depth to the point of rotation O (AASHTO 3.11.5.6); the 20 percent increase is not a factor of safety.
